analyticalQuestion: Does a growing structured low-frequency output set force a square-function defect after one high shell is flattened in critical heat norms?
supportedClaim: For dyadic L and M with H=4LM, one real divergence-free tensor Rudin--Shapiro packet supported in H<=|xi|<2H has M coherent target outputs in the complete first Navier--Stokes Picard iterate. Its heat-Besov and periodic BMO^-1 input norms are O(H^-1/2), while the total first-iterate output is Omega(H^-1), uniformly in the separation H/M=4L and the output count M.

chartContract.takeaway: Output multiplicity and isotropic critical square functions do not force an extra shell factor in the complete first Picard iterate; one tensor sign array flattens both inputs while all matched products remain positive.
